clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby further exempt the said William H. Griffin from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1939." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through July 31, 1939, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when July 31, 1939 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7930 of July 14, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts William H. Griffin from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The recital identifies William H. Griffin as a person who had been exempted for a period of one year ending July 31, 1938, by Executive Order No. 7667 of July 17, 1937; that earlier exemption is a separate instrument, and nothing in it affects when this one ends. The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362904, Common Crawl capture 2025-06-15T01:13:57Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7930, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on July 31, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The OFR catalog search and the held-text name search both report zero hits for this order, so no revoking, superseding or extending instrument is recorded in the packet.

savings.reason: The order grants a permission for a fixed period and contains no saving or transfer provision. What it left behind, William H. Griffin's continued federal employment during the period, accrued while the period ran; no duty or right continues after July 31, 1939 by the order's own terms.
